summary: Story 3 adds an optional, case-insensitive department filter to GET /api/employees and an optional department field on Employee and CreateEmployeeRequest, using the existing in-memory Spring Boot service with no database or new services. Requirements are testable; open questions on blank values, null serialization and locale are recorded as labelled assumptions to confirm at approval. Approval is pending.
decisions: runtime_model: unknown
approval: pending

Current behavior: Employee(id,name,email) and CreateEmployeeRequest(name @NotBlank, email @NotBlank @Email) are records; EmployeeService keeps an in-memory LinkedHashMap with incrementing IDs; GET /api/employees takes no parameters and returns all employees (insertion order); GET by ID returns 404 {error:'Employee not found'}; POST returns 201 or 400 {error:'Invalid employee data'}.
FR1: Add String department to Employee and CreateEmployeeRequest; department is optional on POST (no @NotBlank/@NotNull) so existing clients omitting it still receive 201.
FR2: GET /api/employees accepts an optional query parameter named department.
FR3: When department is supplied, return only employees whose department equals it case-insensitively (e.g. IT, it and It match the same employees).
FR4: When department is omitted, return all employees, identical to current behavior.
FR5: When no employee matches (including unknown departments), return HTTP 200 with an empty JSON array [], never 404.

FR6: GET /api/employees/{id} and POST /api/employees keep existing status codes, error bodies, validation rules and ID assignment for requests without department; employees created without department are still created and returned.

FR7: Swagger/OpenAPI must document the optional department query parameter on GET /api/employees and the department string property in the Employee and CreateEmployeeRequest schemas; docs/api-docs.md should be updated to match (human-review gate preserved).
FR8: Add focused tests for the new behavior and run the full existing regression suite.
AC1: GET /api/employees?department=IT returns exactly the employees with department IT (case-insensitive).
AC2: GET /api/employees?department=it returns a result equivalent to department=IT.
AC3: GET /api/employees returns all employees, including those without a department.
AC4: GET /api/employees?department=<unknown> returns 200 and [].
AC5: POST without department returns 201 and the same validation 400 cases as before; POST with department returns 201 and the response echoes department.
AC6: /v3/api-docs lists the optional department query parameter (type string, not required) on GET /api/employees and department as a string property in Employee and CreateEmployeeRequest.
AC7: All existing and new tests pass.
Constraint: keep implementation minimal and reuse the existing Spring Boot controller/service architecture and in-memory store.
Constraint: no database and no new services.

Constraint: do not modify existing Copilot agents, hooks or Story 1/2 evidence; do not implement before requirements, architecture/design and planning are approved; no commit, push or PR without explicit approval.

Risk (backward compatibility): adding department to the Employee record will add a department field to every Employee JSON response, so existing clients and tests will see "department": null for employees created without one unless null serialization is suppressed.

Risk (existing tests): OpenApiDocumentationTests asserts exact property sets for Employee {id,name,email} and CreateEmployeeRequest {name,email} and exact paths/operations; these assertions will fail once department is added and must be deliberately updated as part of FR8 rather than treated as unintended regressions.

Risk (existing tests): EmployeeApiDocSyncApplicationTests uses a shared Spring context with ID-sensitive assertions (ID 1, empty initial list); new tests that create employees must use @DirtiesContext or equivalent isolation to avoid ordering failures.

Assumption (confirm at approval) - null serialization: the story does not say how a missing department appears in responses; default assumption is that it serializes as null, as Jackson does today, because the story specifies no change. Alternative is omitting the field via non-null inclusion.

Assumption (confirm at approval) - empty/whitespace department filter: the story does not define ?department= (empty) or ?department=%20 (whitespace); default assumption is no special handling, so an empty or blank value is treated as a supplied value that matches no employee and returns 200 []; alternative is treating it as omitted. Matching assumes exact case-insensitive equality with no trimming and no partial or substring matching.

Assumption (confirm at approval) - blank department on POST: the story specifies no validation for department, so empty or whitespace values are accepted and stored as given; null and omitted are equivalent. Employees with a null department never match a supplied filter.

Assumption (confirm at approval) - case-insensitivity locale: the story names no locale; default assumption is locale-independent comparison such as String.equalsIgnoreCase or Locale.ROOT, avoiding default-locale pitfalls like the Turkish dotless i. Full Unicode case folding beyond that is out of scope.

Assumption (confirm at approval) - repeated department parameters (?department=IT&department=HR) are out of scope; standard Spring single-value binding behavior applies and no multi-department filtering is added.
